messages.author: 7a7ed0e90c88eb35
messages.subject: Species ID
parts:
So I will preface this question with a quick summary of what I am doing. We are looking at causes of depredation to Snowy Plover nest. Cameras are set up at sites to take a photo every minute unless motion activate at which point it takes consecutive photos until motion is no longer detected. I am organizing these photos and identifying depredation causes from the photos, by finding the times when consecutive photos were taken in order to identifying if this was the depredation event, as opposed to someone changing the SD card, and what animal caused it. 

I was hoping to be able to create a recordTable from all of the photos in order to find when cameras were motion activated, look at those photos and then ID the species, but it seems the recordTable wants the species to already be identified, the excel file I originally used to create the station directories also list possible depredation causes, should I be connecting the recordTable to this data some how, or am I going about this the wrong way and should be doing something else, maybe go back to another step and redo it or something?Is there a way to ID species after the recordTable is created? Any input would be much appreciated!! 

Here is a copy of the code I used to create the recordTable (images have been renamed by datetimeOriginals):
recordTable2015 <- recordTable(inDir = "2015renamed", IDfrom = "directory", minDeltaTime = 0, timeZone = "America/Los_Angeles", writecsv = FALSE)

The table shows the Station and Species as being the same.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Species ID
parts:
You are right, currently images need to be identified to be returned by recordTable. From what I see you are using species directories to identify images. Here's a little workaround you could use.
1. give all images some pseudo-ID (create some dummy species folder and put all images in there, for each station separately)
2. run exifTagNames to find the metadata field containing information whether camera was motion-triggered or in time-lapse mode (trigger mode in Reconyx)
3. run recordTable (minDeltaTime = 0), and have the function return the metadata field for the trigger mode
4. subset all motion-triggered pictures and move these to back to the respective station directory
5. do your identification
6. re-run recordTable, with argument exclude set to the dummy directory created in step 1.

It is a bit cumbersome, but the only way I can think of now.

In my sample images, I could not use digiKam to filter images for the trigger mode. If that should be possible, it might be another option.

Can you elaborate please on the second question about the other table you want to connect the record table with?
